messages.content: Quick Texas update: San Antonio sent the load-in map and exhibitor arrival is earlier than we thought. Also the Austin hotel clarified that hot breakfast is later than my first campus-adjacent appointment Wednesday. Can you tighten the Tuesday-to-Friday timeline without changing the booked flights, car, or rooms?

Yes. I would keep the bookings and adjust the operating plan: Tuesday is a pack-and-drive day, Wednesday is grab-and-go only, Thursday gets an earlier venue arrival, and Friday stays airport-first. The key change is not letting breakfast or a sit-down lunch become the timekeeper. For Tuesday, build the drive around the Fort Worth stop and get south before afternoon traffic; for Friday, aim to have the rental physically returned around 10:15 for the 12:55 SAT departure.
For Wednesday, should I still try for the Austin breakfast if they have coffee out early?

Coffee is fine, but I would not plan on the hotel breakfast as food. Buy a yogurt, bar, or breakfast sandwich Tuesday night near the Arboretum, pack the car before bed, and check out before the first visit. Luggage can stay in the covered cargo area while you are on campus.
What does Tuesday look like minute by minute?

Leave Richardson about 7:15. Fort Worth check-in by 8:30. Depart Fort Worth around 11:15 if you can, quick lunch or fuel on the south side, then I-35 toward Austin. Target Austin hotel arrival 3:45-4:15 so you are not checking in hungry and rushed.
And Thursday? The fair may not wrap until 8:30.

For the San Antonio fair, arrive at the venue by 4:15 with the new map, not 4:45. Bring a snack for the table. Afterward, use the North Star or airport-area dinner backup rather than driving across town; choose somewhere still serving until at least 9:30.
Give me the Friday airport plan too. I do not want the Atlanta connection squeezed because I wandered over breakfast.

Friday plan: check out by 8:50, skip any sit-down breakfast, fuel by 9:15, head straight to SAT rental return, and target car return 10:00-10:15. That leaves time for final receipt, bag drop, security, and the 12:55 flight. Put hotel folio, fuel receipt, tolls, car receipt, and any parking receipts in the finance folder before boarding.

messages.content: Texas is wrapped up, so I need to start the late-October Upper Midwest loop. Draft is Sunday SLC to the Chicago area, Monday suburban high-school visits plus an evening fair near Oak Brook, Tuesday morning counselor breakfast in Madison, Wednesday Milwaukee high-school appointments, and a Thursday late-afternoon counselor meetup now planned around Wauwatosa. Can you compare Chicago round-trip versus flying into Chicago and home from Milwaukee, and tell me if I should keep a rental car the whole time? I also need hotel bases that won’t leave me stranded for dinner.

I can. Before I rank it: what are the rough fair end time Monday, the Thursday meetup end time, and are you planning to fly home Friday rather than Thursday night? Also, any nightly hotel ceiling I should use for the first pass?

Assume Monday fair ends around 8:15, Thursday runs 4:30 to 6:30, and I want to fly home Friday. Sunday departure can be after lunch because I have a morning handoff. For hotels, I would like to stay around $240 before tax when possible. Breakfast included is helpful, but I care more about not having a silly drive before a 7 or 8 a.m. event. Delta is nice from SLC if the schedule is comparable, but do not force it.

Then Chicago-in and Milwaukee-out is the cleaner working plan. Quick comparison: Chicago round-trip is probably cheaper by roughly $150-$250 after fare differences, but it adds a Wauwatosa-to-Chicago backtrack Thursday night or a Friday morning drive to O'Hare, plus tolls and weather risk. Chicago-in/Milwaukee-out may cost more and may add a one-way car fee, but it protects Thursday evening, reduces fatigue, and keeps Friday simpler. I would keep one rental car from Chicago pickup to Milwaukee return; trains and rideshares look fussy for Oak Brook, Madison, and suburban Milwaukee with materials and luggage.
For Chicago, would you aim for O'Hare or Midway?

O'Hare is my first choice because it usually has more SLC afternoon choices, more rental inventory, and an easier angle to Oak Brook. Midway is workable if it has a clearly better nonstop or fare, but I would not take Midway just to save a small amount. For the car, the one-way fee is acceptable if it is visible upfront and not much over the cost of the extra gas, tolls, and time of backtracking.
Can you sketch the hotel nights? I do not want the Madison breakfast ruined by a 5 a.m. drive from Oak Brook.

Best sequence on the draft times: Sunday night Oak Brook or Oakbrook Terrace; Monday after the fair, drive to Madison and sleep near the breakfast venue; Tuesday night Madison again if Wednesday appointments start later, or Milwaukee/Wauwatosa if Wednesday starts early; Wednesday and Thursday nights in Wauwatosa, Brookfield, or Milwaukee West. The only awkward piece is the Monday late drive to Madison, but it is still better than leaving Oak Brook before dawn Tuesday.
How bad is that Monday drive after the fair? Would Rockford make more sense?

Oak Brook to Madison after 8:30 p.m. is usually about 2 hours 10 minutes to 2 hours 30 minutes, so you could arrive around 10:45 or 11:00. Rockford splits the pain, but it creates a Tuesday morning drive of about 1 hour 10 minutes before a breakfast event, which is the wrong side of the trade-off. I would only use Rockford if Madison rates are unreasonable or late check-in is a problem.
Okay, Madison Monday. I will need food that night.

Do not count on a real dinner after arriving in Madison. Eat something near Oak Brook before leaving if the fair food is light, and keep a sandwich or protein box in the car. For the Madison hotel, I would favor late check-in, a lobby market, and at least one nearby restaurant or delivery option over a prettier location.
What flight options would you shortlist?

Outbound Sunday: shortlist a 1-3 p.m. SLC to O'Hare nonstop if the fare is reasonable; a similar United or American nonstop is fine if it lands earlier or costs materially less; keep a Midway option only as a price check. Return Friday from Milwaukee: look for one-stop itineraries through MSP, Detroit, Atlanta, Denver, or Chicago with a comfortable connection. I would avoid very early departures because they waste the benefit of staying near Wauwatosa, and I would avoid anything with two stops unless finance forces it.
Rank the return choices. I would rather not get home too late, but connection quality matters more than carrier.

Ranking for now: first, a late-morning or early-afternoon MKE-SLC one-stop with about 70-100 minutes to connect; second, a midafternoon MKE-SLC with a longer but not absurd connection if the first option gets too tight; third, driving to O'Hare for a cheaper or nonstop return; last, a pre-8 a.m. Milwaukee departure or any two-stop routing. The Chicago return needs a big savings to justify the backtrack.
Give me hotel areas or examples to hold, not final bookings yet.

Oak Brook: look at Oakbrook Terrace or Oak Brook proper near the fair, with free parking and food nearby; Hyatt House, Hilton Garden Inn, or a comparable Marriott/Hilton property would be practical. Madison: first choice is downtown or near the UW/counselor breakfast if the rate is tolerable; Hampton Inn downtown or a campus-adjacent Hilton/Marriott works if late check-in is confirmed. If rates spike, Middleton is the backup, but it adds morning drive time. Milwaukee: Wauwatosa, Brookfield, or Milwaukee West near Mayfair/Research Park; Residence Inn, SpringHill Suites, or a similar property with breakfast and parking would fit the logistics.
What deadlines should I put on the calendar?

Put three holds on a calendar: flights by fare-lock expiration, hotels by each refundable cancellation cutoff, and car by any free-cancel deadline. I would also set a reminder 10 days out to release the Chicago round-trip benchmark if the open-jaw premium is still reasonable, and another reminder 72 hours before travel to recheck breakfast times, parking, and late arrival notes.
Can you summarize the recommendation for the approval request?

Recommended plan for approval: fly SLC to Chicago on Sunday afternoon, preferably into O'Hare unless Midway is clearly better; rent one car in Chicago and return it in Milwaukee; fly home Friday from MKE. This costs more than a Chicago round-trip but avoids the Thursday night or Friday morning backtrack after Wauwatosa, reduces fatigue, and protects the Madison breakfast. Hotel sequence: Oak Brook/Oakbrook Terrace Sunday, Madison Monday and likely Tuesday, Wauwatosa or Milwaukee West Wednesday-Thursday. Meal notes: eat or pack dinner before the Monday Madison drive, verify breakfast hours at Madison and Wauwatosa hotels, and choose properties with nearby restaurants rather than isolated highway stays.

messages.content: Upper Midwest updates: Madison breakfast moved to 7:20 a.m., Oak Brook added a counselor reception before the fair floor opens, and the Milwaukee meetup moved from downtown to a west-side campus venue. The Chicago inbound still works Sunday afternoon. Friday MKE-SLC has one midday one-stop that makes the morning feel tight, and a later one with a long connection. Can you rank those and reset the hotel sequence?

Yes. With the Madison breakfast at 7:20, I would protect the Monday-night Madison stay. With the Thursday venue on the west side, I would lean toward Wauwatosa or Brookfield for the Milwaukee nights. The open question is Tuesday night: stay in Madison to avoid another check-in, or move to Wauwatosa to make Wednesday morning easier. Do you have any Friday morning appointment, or is it just airport day?
No Friday visits, just return. I can leave a Wauwatosa hotel by 9:15 if needed. I would rather avoid a connection under an hour.

Then rank the returns this way: 1) Midday MKE-SLC if the connection is at least about 65-70 minutes; leave Wauwatosa 9:15, fuel, return the car by 10:15, and keep the afternoon arrival. 2) Later MKE-SLC with the longer connection if the midday option drops below that connection window or prices oddly high. 3) Chicago return only as a finance benchmark, because the drive back undercuts the whole route.

Hotel availability: Oak Brook is still fine. Hampton near UW has two rooms left at $258, breakfast 6:00, parking $18. Hilton Garden in Middleton is $199 but breakfast is not included. Residence Inn Milwaukee West is $219 with breakfast. Brookfield Marriott is $185, no breakfast.

For a 7:20 UW-area breakfast, I would hold the Hampton despite the price and parking. The Middleton savings can disappear quickly once you add breakfast, parking math, and the earlier drive. For Milwaukee, Residence Inn West is the better operational hold; included breakfast and west-side access are worth more here than the lower Brookfield rate.
The Madison breakfast is near campus, and I can leave Madison around 2:30 Tuesday after two counselor calls.

That makes the sequence clear: Sunday Oak Brook; Monday late drive to Madison and stay near UW; Tuesday after the counselor calls, drive to Wauwatosa/Milwaukee West and stay there Tuesday through Thursday. It adds a Tuesday check-in, but it removes a Wednesday morning Madison-to-Milwaukee drive and places you near the Thursday venue.
Is that too much hotel churn?

It is one more move than staying Madison Tuesday, but it pays for itself. If you stay Madison Tuesday, Wednesday starts with a 75-90 minute drive before school visits. Moving Tuesday afternoon uses a lower-pressure window and gives you predictable mornings Wednesday through Friday.
Breakfast backups?

Tuesday: use the Hampton breakfast at 6:00, but carry a bar in case the room is crowded. Wednesday and Thursday: Residence Inn breakfast should work unless a school visit starts very early; buy one backup item Tuesday night. Friday: grab coffee only if it is quick, then airport timeline first.
Late dinners?

Monday is the risky one. Eat in Oak Brook before leaving or pack dinner; do not depend on Madison restaurants at 11 p.m. Tuesday and Wednesday are easier around Mayfair, Brookfield, and Milwaukee West, so choose dinner close to the hotel and avoid downtown detours.
Give me the holds and action list.

Holds to place: keep the Sunday afternoon SLC-Chicago inbound, preferably O'Hare; keep Chicago pickup and Milwaukee return on the rental with the one-way fee visible; hold Oak Brook Sunday, Hampton near UW Monday, and Residence Inn Milwaukee West Tuesday-Thursday. Return flight: take the midday MKE-SLC one-stop if the connection stays at 65-70 minutes or better; otherwise use the later one-stop rather than backtracking to Chicago. Action reminders: confirm Monday late check-in in Madison, verify breakfast start times, release the Middleton/Brookfield backups once the main holds are confirmed, keep the Chicago round-trip only as a finance comparison, and set Friday car return target around 10:15.
